input.question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?
input.ground_truth: There are development languages that are cross platform. This is one way this can be accomplished. The same code base will run in various environments (Linux/BSD/Windows) and then OS specific code can be ran inside the software that is called based on what environment the code detects. Also, a second way would be runtime emulation such as WINE, but I don't think that is what you are referring to

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and you want to play with it in your house and also take it to your friend’s house. But your house has a wooden floor and your friend’s house has carpet. The way the toy car moves is a little different on each floor, but it’s still the same toy car, and you can still play with it.

Now, think of the toy car as a program (like a game or an app), and the floors are like different operating systems (like Windows, Mac, or Android). The program is written in a special way so it can work on different floors (operating systems), even though each floor is a little different. Sometimes, the program needs a tiny helper (called an “interpreter” or “virtual machine”) to make sure it can play nicely on any floor.

So, the same program can run on different operating systems because it’s made in a way that it can understand and work with each one, just like your toy car can roll on both wood and carpet!
